theory.intro: A parallelogram can be cut and rearranged into a rectangle with the same base and height, so its area is base times perpendicular height.
facts: **Area $=$ base $\times$ height**, where height is the **perpendicular** distance between the base and the opposite side.
The height is **not** the slanted side; it is measured at a right angle to the base.
Area is measured in square units: cm$^{2}$, m$^{2}$.
steps: Identify the base and the perpendicular height (the dashed line at a right angle).
Write the answer with squared units.

foundation.solution_text:
The perpendicular height is still $6\text{ cm}$, even though it meets the base line outside the shape.
$A=bh$
$=11\times6$
$=66\text{ cm}^{2}$

foundation.question_text: A parallelogram-shaped floor tile has a base of $20\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $12\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the tile in $\text{cm}^{2}$.

development.solution_text:
The dashed height $8\text{ cm}$ is perpendicular to the $6\text{ cm}$ side, so that side is the base. The $9\text{ cm}$ slanted side is not used.
$A=bh$
$=6\times8$
$=48\text{ cm}^{2}$

The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side is $8\text{ m}$.
$A=bh$
$=13\times8$
$=104\text{ m}^{2}$

development.question_text: A wall in the shape of a parallelogram has a base of $30\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $10\text{ m}$. One litre of paint covers $5\text{ m}^{2}$. How many litres of paint are needed to cover the wall?
development.solution_text:
$A=bh$
$=30\times10$
$=300\text{ m}^{2}$
$300\div5=60$
$60$ litres of paint are needed.

mastery.question_text: Parallelogram $P$ has a base of $18\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $7\text{ cm}$. Parallelogram $Q$ has a base of $14\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $9\text{ cm}$. Which has the larger area, and by how many $\text{cm}^{2}$?
mastery.solution_text:
$A_{P}=18\times7$
$=126\text{ cm}^{2}$
$A_{Q}=14\times9$
$=126\text{ cm}^{2}$
Neither is larger: both parallelograms have an area of $126\text{ cm}^{2}$.

mastery.question_text: A garden bed shaped like a parallelogram has a base of $6.5\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $4\text{ m}$. Mulch costs $\$18$ per square metre. Find the cost of mulching the garden bed.

A parallelogram has a base of $8\text{ cm}$ and a perpendicular height of $5\text{ cm}$. Both the base and the perpendicular height are tripled. Find the new area in $\text{cm}^{2}$ and state how many times as large it is as the original.
mastery.solution_text:
$A_{\text{old}}=8\times5$
$=40\text{ cm}^{2}$
New base $24\text{ cm}$, new height $15\text{ cm}$.
$A_{\text{new}}=24\times15$
$=360\text{ cm}^{2}$
$360\div40=9$
The new area is $360\text{ cm}^{2}$, which is $9$ times the original.
